items.title: Strong spectral commutation of self-adjoint operators
items.statement:
**(a) Setting.** Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral theorem. Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A$ and $B$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$
with domains $D(A)$ and $D(B)$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). By the spectral
theorem each of them has a unique spectral projection-valued measure on the
Borel sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]); write $E_{A}$
for the spectral projection-valued measure of $A$ and $E_{B}$ for that of $B$.

**(b) Strong spectral commutation.** The operators $A$ and $B$ **strongly
commute**, or are **spectrally compatible**, when their spectral
projection-valued measures commute on every pair of Borel sets:
$$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)\qquad\text{for all Borel }\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is the relation that the term "compatible sharp observables" abbreviates
on the physical pages of the category. It is a condition on the two families
of projections, not on a single vector or on a formal difference of operator
products.

**(c) Not to be confused with a commutator identity on a dense invariant
domain.** Let $D$ be a dense linear subspace of $D(A)\cap D(B)$ such that
$AD\subseteq D$ and $BD\subseteq D$. Then $ABu$ and $BAu$ are defined for every
$u\in D$. Strong spectral commutation implies $ABu=BAu$ on $D$: Teschl's
bounded Borel calculus for a strongly commuting pair gives, for each bounded
Borel function $h$, $h(B)D(A)\subseteq D(A)$ and $Ah(B)x=h(B)Ax$ for
$x\in D(A)$ (Section 4.2, Lemma 4.5). Apply this with
$h_n(\lambda)=\lambda\mathbf 1_{[-n,n]}(\lambda)$. For $u\in D$, both $u$ and
$Au$ belong to $D(B)$, so the spectral theorem gives $h_n(B)u\to Bu$ and
$h_n(B)Au\to BAu$. Since $Ah_n(B)u=h_n(B)Au$ and $A$ is closed, it follows
that $Bu\in D(A)$ and $ABu=BAu$. The converse can fail even for a dense
common invariant domain: the examples page records a pair of self-adjoint
extensions for which the commutator vanishes on such a domain but the spectral
projections do not commute.

For bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint $A$ and $B$, if the commutator
vanishes on a dense $D$, boundedness extends $AB=BA$ to all of $H$; the bounded
Borel calculus then makes this equivalent to strong spectral commutation
(Teschl, Section 4.2, Corollary 4.7). No graph-norm core property is needed in
the comparison above. Clause (b), rather than a domain commutator identity, is
the definition governing joint sharp outcomes.

**(d) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) fix a definition and a comparison of
conditions. They assert no physical claim, no joint measurement, no
simultaneous sharp value and no dynamical statement. All further content about
strong spectral commutation used by the category -- the bounded-calculus
consequences, the joint projection-valued measure criterion and the physical
readings -- is established as separate results with their own hypotheses.

items.title: The Schroedinger-Robertson bound in anticommutator form and the Robertson bound on product domains
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A,B$ be symmetric
densely defined operators on $H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$
with $\|u\|=1$ satisfy in addition $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, that is
$Bu\in D(A)$ and $Au\in D(B)$. Put
$$a:=\langle Au,u\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle Bu,u\rangle,\qquad x:=(A-a)u,\qquad y:=(B-b)u,\qquad \Delta A:=\|x\|,\qquad \Delta B:=\|y\|,$$
and write $\{A,B\}u:=ABu+BAu$ and $[A,B]u:=ABu-BAu$ for the pairings at $u$.
Then:

(a) $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $x,y\in H$, and
$$\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\bigr\rangle=\tfrac12\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-ab, \qquad \langle[A,B]u,u\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle ;$$

(b) *(Robertson bound)* $\Delta A\,\Delta B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|$;

(c) *(Schroedinger-Robertson bound)*
$$(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge\Bigl(\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\bigr\rangle\Bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|^{2},$$
that is, with the expanded anticommutator pairing
$(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge\bigl(\tfrac12\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-ab\bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|^{2}$;

(d) equality holds in (c) if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent;
in particular the Robertson bound (b) follows from (c) because the first
square is nonnegative;

(e) if $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators, then
the product-domain hypothesis $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$ holds for every unit
$u\in H$ and clauses (a)-(d) apply to every unit $u$.

No energy-time inequality and no apparatus statement is made.

items.title: Preparation variance and spread of an assigned sharp observable
items.statement:
**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with
declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation
$\rho$, in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean
$m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second
moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome
law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$
read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation
spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in
the unit $u_{A}$. When either quantity is not finite the variance and the
spread of the pair in $\rho$ are **not defined**; the definition does not
extend them by $+\infty$.

**(c) Values and hypotheses.** The variance and its hypotheses are exactly
those of the moment theorem: for a pure preparation of a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$,
equal to $\bigl(\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$
when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$; for a preparation $\rho$ the identities and existence
criteria are those of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]]. In particular a mean exists
exactly when $\rho$ is concentrated on the domain of $|A|^{1/2}$ in the sense
of those items, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments
automatically.

**(d) Products of spreads.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$
and $(B,u_{B})$ in a common preparation $\rho$ in which both spreads are
defined, the product $\Delta_{\rho}A\,\Delta_{\rho}B$ is a nonnegative real
number read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; for a pure preparation of a unit
vector in $D(A)\cap D(B)$ it is
$\|(A-a)\psi\|\,\|(B-b)\psi\|$ with the real means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$.

**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.

The item fixes terminology and readings of P1 and P2 only; it asserts no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance, no joint measurement, no dynamics and no empirical result, and it does not claim that any preparation has finite moments automatically.

items.title: Bounded Borel calculus of strongly commuting self-adjoint operators
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space and let $A,B$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$ with
spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$ that strongly commute in the
sense of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b):
$$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)\qquad\text{for all Borel }\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
For a bounded Borel function $h$ write $h(A):=\int h\,dE_{A}$ and
$h(B):=\int h\,dE_{B}$ for its operators under the bounded Borel functional
calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). Then:

(a) for all bounded Borel $f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$,
$$f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A);$$

(b) for every bounded Borel $f$ one has $f(B)D(A)\subseteq D(A)$, and
$$A\,f(B)x=f(B)Ax\qquad\text{for every }x\in D(A);$$
the same statement holds with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged, and it is
also true with $f(B)$ replaced by any bounded linear combination or norm limit
of bounded Borel functions of $B$;

(c) for every bounded Borel $f$ the bounded operator $f(B)$ commutes with all
spectral projections of $A$: $f(B)E_{A}(\Lambda)=E_{A}(\Lambda)f(B)$ for every
Borel $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R$. Consequently, for real-valued bounded Borel
$f$ the pair $(f(A),B)$ strongly commutes: the map
$F(\Lambda):=E_{A}(f^{-1}(\Lambda))$ is a projection-valued measure on the
Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ representing the bounded self-adjoint operator
$f(A)$, and $F(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)F(\Lambda)$ for all Borel
$\Lambda,\Sigma$; hence also $(f(A),g(B))$ strongly commutes for real-valued
bounded Borel $f,g$.

items.title: Strong spectral commutation, joint projection-valued measures and bounded Borel calculus
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space and let $A,B$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$ with
spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then the following are equivalent:

(i) $A$ and $B$ strongly commute in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b), that is
$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)$ for all Borel
$\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(ii) there is a regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel
sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R^{2}$ whose values on measurable rectangles
([[def-measurable-rectangle]]) are
$G(\Lambda\times\Sigma)=E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)$, and whose marginals are
$G(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=E_{A}(\Lambda)$ and
$G(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)$;

(iii) $f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$ for all bounded Borel functions
$f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$, where the operators are those of the bounded
Borel functional calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]).

If these conditions hold, the projection-valued measure $G$ of (ii) is unique,
and for all bounded Borel $f,g$ one has the representation
$$f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}f(a)g(b)\,dG(a,b).$$

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Chapter 3, printed pages 87-100 (PDF pages 99-112): projection-valued measures, the spectral theorem and the joint calculus of commuting spectral projections

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', Sections 7-8, printed pages 16-19: simultaneous diagonalization of commuting Hermitian operators and complete sets of commuting observables

items.title: The position-momentum commutator identity on the product domain
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space with the componentwise position and momentum operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clauses (a) and (b), with domains
$$D(Q_{j})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},\qquad D(P_{k})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},$$
and let $D_{k}$ denote the weak partial derivative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]). Then:

(a) *Product rule.* If $f\in H^{(r)}$ has $x_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ (the latter read
componentwise), then $x_{j}f$ lies in $D(P_{j})$ and
$$D_{j}(x_{j}f)=f+x_{j}D_{j}f;$$

(b) *The product domain.* $D(Q_{j}P_{j})=\{f\in D(P_{j}):\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$
and $D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\{f\in D(Q_{j}):\ D_{j}(x_{j}f)\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$,
and their intersection is
$$D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{j}f,\ x_{j}f,\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\};$$

(c) *Commutator identity.* For every $f\in D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$,
$$(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})f=i\hbar\,f;$$

(d) *Core.* The componentwise Schwartz class
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]])
is contained in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$, and (c) holds on it.

No identity of unbounded products is asserted outside $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$;
in particular no identity is asserted on $D(P_{j})$ alone.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58 (PDF pages 67-70): position and momentum operators, dense domains and the canonical commutation relation
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 2.3.1-2.3.2, printed pages 26-27 (PDF pages 34-35): the commutator [x,p]=i hbar computed on differentiable wavefunctions

items.title: Approximation of Q-P graph-domain vectors by product-domain vectors
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, and let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
with the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. Let
$\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ with $\psi\ne0$ be a class and let
$D_{P}:=D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$ be the product domain characterized in
[[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-commutator-identity]] clause (b). Then
there is a sequence $(\varphi_{n})_{n\ge1}\subseteq D_{P}$ with
$$\varphi_{n}\to\frac{\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{Q_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{P_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad \|\varphi_{n}\|=1$$
in $H^{(r)}$. In particular, if $\psi$ is a unit vector, then
$\varphi_{n}\to\psi$, $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi$ and
$P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to P_{j}\psi$ in norm, and consequently
$$\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|,\qquad \langle P_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle P_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|P_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|P_{j}\psi\| .$$

items.title: The Robertson relation for preparation spreads of assigned sharp observables
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ and $(B,u_{B})$ be assigned sharp
observables with outcome laws $\mu^{A},\mu^{B}$ and let
$\Delta_{\rho}A,\Delta_{\rho}B$ be their preparation spreads in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Let $\psi$ be a unit vector.
Whenever $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, put
$$a:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle.$$
Then:

(a) **Weak form.** If $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, then the means $a,b$ are real,
the spreads $\Delta_{\psi}A$ and $\Delta_{\psi}B$ are defined, both are read in
the units $u_{A}$ and $u_{B}$, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\bigl|\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle\bigr| .$$

(b) **Robertson form.** If in addition $\psi\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, that is
$B\psi\in D(A)$ and $A\psi\in D(B)$, then the pairing
$\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle:=\langle AB\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle BA\psi,\psi\rangle$
is defined, is purely imaginary, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr| ,$$
read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; moreover the anticommutator refinement
$$(\Delta_{\psi}A)^{2}(\Delta_{\psi}B)^{2}\ge\Bigl(\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}\psi,\psi\bigr\rangle\Bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr|^{2}$$
holds, with equality in the refined bound if and only if $(A-a)\psi$ and
$(B-b)\psi$ are linearly dependent.

(c) **Bounded observables.** If $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined
self-adjoint operators, then clauses (a) and (b) hold for every unit
$\psi\in H$ with all hypotheses automatic ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

(d) **Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1
and P2 and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two outcome
laws in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law, no apparatus
resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, and no
time observable. In particular no energy-time inequality is asserted, and
clauses (a)-(c) do not claim that a laboratory procedure realizes either
observable or attains the bounds; whether a concrete preparation and apparatus
realize the pair $(A,u_{A})$ and produce the spread $\Delta_{\psi}A$ is a
tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

The statement is a conditional consequence of P1 and P2 and the cited mathematics; it concerns preparation spreads of outcome laws only, and asserts no apparatus error, no disturbance, no joint measurement, no energy-time inequality and no empirical result.

items.title: The position-momentum preparation relation of the massive spin-s model
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the
internal-factor assignment P6 of the framework, read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q_{j},P_{j}$ be the model's $j$-th position and
$j$-th momentum operators with their maximal domains, and let
$\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$ and $\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$ be their preparation spreads in
the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Let
$\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ be a unit vector and put
$$a:=\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle P_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad x:=(Q_{j}-a)\psi,\qquad y:=(P_{j}-b)\psi .$$
Then:

(a) $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$ and $\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$ are defined and
$$\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\,\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}\ge\frac{\hbar}{2};$$

(b) if in addition $\psi\in D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$, then
$(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})\psi=i\hbar\psi$ and the bound of (a) follows from the
Robertson relation for the two observables;

(c) for every unit $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ the centered pairing has the
exact imaginary part
$$\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=-\frac{\hbar}{2};$$
consequently equality $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}=\hbar/2$ holds if
and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent and
$\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=0$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P5, P6 and the cited
mathematics. It concerns the two separately assigned position and momentum
outcome laws in one preparation, needs no hypothesis on the products
$Q_{j}P_{j}$ or $P_{j}Q_{j}$. The compatibility results of this page show that
no joint sharp observable with the exact spectral marginals of $Q_{j}$ and
$P_{j}$ exists; this statement makes no claim about existence or
nonexistence of unsharp joint measurements or their outcome laws. It asserts
no apparatus realization, no disturbance relation, no dynamics and no
empirical result. Massless, relativistic, singular-potential and boundary
realizations are separate models for which no such relation is asserted.

items.title: Compatible sharp observables, their joint law and the ideal joint instrument
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the ideal
conditional measurement postulate P3 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ and $(B,u_{B})$ be assigned sharp
observables with spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). Call a regular
projection-valued measure $H$ on the Borel sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R^{2}$ a
**joint sharp observable** of the pair when its marginals are the two spectral
measures,
$$H(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=E_{A}(\Lambda),\qquad H(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)\qquad(\Lambda,\Sigma\ \text{Borel}),$$
and call the pair **compatible** when such an $H$ exists. Then:

(a) **Criterion.** The pair is compatible if and only if $A$ and $B$ strongly
commute in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b), if and only if
$f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$ for all bounded Borel $f,g$; the joint sharp observable
$H$ is then unique, and for bounded Borel $f,g$
$$f(A)g(B)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}f(a)g(b)\,dH(a,b) .$$

(b) **Joint outcome law.** If the pair is compatible, then for every
preparation $\rho$ the assignment
$$\mu^{H}_{\rho}(S):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,H(S)\bigr)\qquad(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{2}\ \text{Borel})$$
is a probability measure on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R^{2}$, the **joint
outcome law** of the pair in $\rho$, and its marginals are the individual
laws:
$$\mu^{H}_{\rho}(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\Lambda),\qquad \mu^{H}_{\rho}(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=\mu^{B}_{\rho}(\Sigma) .$$
For the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ it reads
$\mu^{H}_{\psi}(S)=\|H(S)\psi\|^{2}$.

(c) **Ideal finite-resolution joint instrument.** If the pair is compatible
and $(P_{1},\dots,P_{n})$, $(Q_{1},\dots,Q_{m})$ are the projections of two
finite disjoint Borel partitions of $\mathbb R$,
$P_{i}:=E_{A}(\Lambda_{i})$, $Q_{j}:=E_{B}(\Sigma_{j})$ with
$\bigcup_{i}\Lambda_{i}=\bigcup_{j}\Sigma_{j}=\mathbb R$, then
$R_{ij}:=H(\Lambda_{i}\times\Sigma_{j})=P_{i}Q_{j}$ are mutually orthogonal
projections with strong sum $I$, and in the framework's declared ideal sharp
measurement of the family $(R_{ij})$ the outcome probabilities are
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$ with marginals $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{i})$
and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho Q_{j})$. For each joint outcome $(i,j)$ with
$p_{ij}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})>0$, the sequential declared ideal
measurements of $(P_{i})$ and then $(Q_{j})$, or in the reverse order, give the
same conditional state
$$\rho_{ij}=\frac{R_{ij}\rho R_{ij}}{p_{ij}}=\frac{Q_{j}P_{i}\rho P_{i}Q_{j}}{p_{ij}}=\frac{P_{i}Q_{j}\rho Q_{j}P_{i}}{p_{ij}}.$$
In that state an immediate repetition of the joint measurement or either
corresponding marginal-bin measurement returns the same outcome with
probability one. If $p_{ij}=0$, no conditional state or repeatability claim is
made for that outcome.

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P3 and
the cited mathematics. A joint sharp observable, when it exists, is a
mathematical object of the framework: it supplies a joint outcome law, not an
apparatus. Clause (c)'s updates and repeatability are conditional ideal-model
claims under P3; no universal disturbance relation or apparatus-level
disturbance claim is asserted. The claim that a concrete laboratory device
realizes the joint measurement, with its resolution, losses and systematics, is
a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus postulate P7. No dynamics or empirical result is asserted.

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 3.4, printed pages 81-84 (PDF pages 84-87): commuting observables, simultaneous eigenfunctions, simultaneous values and the non-degeneracy caveat in the textbook argument

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Chapter 3, printed pages 87-100 (PDF pages 99-112): spectral projections, the multiplication form of the spectral theorem and the calculus of commuting projections

The statement is a conditional consequence of P1, P2, P3 and the cited mathematics; the update and repeatability claims are consequences inside the ideal instrument model, not universal or apparatus-level disturbance claims. items.title: Position and momentum of the massive model have no joint sharp observable
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment P6, read
for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a coordinate index $j$. Then:

(a) the spectral projection-valued measures $E_{Q_{j}}$ and $E_{P_{j}}$ of the
model's $j$-th position and $j$-th momentum do not strongly commute: there are
Borel sets $\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$E_{Q_{j}}(\Lambda)E_{P_{j}}(\Sigma)\ne E_{P_{j}}(\Sigma)E_{Q_{j}}(\Lambda)$;

(b) consequently the pair $(Q_{j},P_{j})$ is not compatible: there is no regular
projection-valued measure $H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R^{2}$ whose
marginals are $E_{Q_{j}}$ and $E_{P_{j}}$, and in particular the framework
assigns to the pair no joint sharp outcome law in any preparation;

(c) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5, P6 and the cited
mathematics and concerns the model's assigned sharp operators only. It does
not assert that no approximate or unsharp joint measurement exists, gives no
error-disturbance relation, and records no apparatus or empirical result.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', Sections 7-8, printed pages 16-19: simultaneous diagonalization of commuting Hermitian operators

items.title: What the uncertainty and compatibility page adopts, proves and does not claim
items.statement:
## Scope of the page

**Adopted, not restated.** The physical content of this page is the state and
composition postulate P1 and the observable and probability postulate P2 in
the vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] for the
position and momentum statements). The page adopts no further physical
assumption beyond the model postulates P5 and P6 used to name $Q_{j}$ and
$P_{j}$; the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem are carried explicitly
in every mathematical item.

**What is proved.** [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] fixes the
reading of preparation variance and spread.
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] proves the weak Robertson bound
for unit vectors in both domains, the Robertson bound and its anticommutator
refinement on the product domains, and the automatic validity for bounded
observables. [[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-relation]] proves
$\Delta Q_{j}\Delta P_{j}\ge\hbar/2$ on the full maximal domain of the pair,
with the exact imaginary part $-\hbar/2$ and the equality characterization.
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]],
[[thm-nrqm-uncertainty-joint-pvm-criterion]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-compatible-sharp-observables-and-joint-law]] fix
strong spectral commutation, prove its equivalence with the existence and
uniqueness of a joint sharp observable and give the joint law with its
marginals; [[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-incompatible]] proves
that the model's position and momentum are incompatible. All of these are
conditional consequences of the postulates and the cited mathematics.

**What is not claimed.** No item of this page asserts an apparatus resolution,
a measurement error, a disturbance of the preparation, an approximate or
unsharp joint measurement, a joint position-momentum law, a time observable or
a universal energy-time inequality. The inequalities concern the spreads of
the outcome laws of one preparation; they are not statements about the
precision of a laboratory procedure, and the equalities of the position and
momentum item are properties of specific preparations, not of every state. The
identification of a preparation and an apparatus with the model's states and
operators is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation
and apparatus postulate P7; neither the postulates nor the theorems here
report a measured value, a trial count or a statistical inference. Agreement
of the conditional predictions with data would test the combined model and
apparatus assumptions; it is not established or claimed here.

**Distinctions preserved.** The page keeps preparation spread, apparatus
resolution and disturbance separate throughout; it also keeps the mathematical
identity $[A,B]u=0$ on a dense core separate from strong spectral commutation.
The examples companion records a domain-sensitive counterexample, the Gaussian
family that saturates the position-momentum bound, the spin-$\tfrac12$ spread
account, the energy-time scope remark and the error-disturbance distinction.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 3.4 and 3.4.1, printed pages 81-88 (PDF pages 84-91): commuting observables and simultaneous values, with the non-degeneracy caveat, and the position-momentum uncertainty relation with its Gaussian saturation

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', printed pages 1-19: uncertainty defined, the uncertainty inequality and its saturation conditions, the energy-time discussion with time as a parameter, and simultaneous diagonalization of commuting observables

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Sections 2.1, 3.1 and 8.1, printed pages 55-58, 87-100 and 173-175 (PDF pages 67-70, 99-112, 185-187): self-adjoint operators, spectral measures and generators of one-parameter groups

items.physical_scope: A scope audit of the uncertainty and compatibility page: it records P1 and P2 in the framework's vocabulary, the P5/P6 model assignments used for position and momentum, and P3 solely for the compatible-observables item's stipulated ideal finite-bin Lüders updates on positive-probability outcomes. The page proves conditional preparation-spread inequalities and spectral-compatibility criteria; it rules out only a joint sharp position-momentum observable with the exact spectral marginals and makes no claim about unsharp joint laws. It asserts no universal disturbance relation or concrete-apparatus disturbance claim, dynamics, empirical value or experimental finding. It proves nothing itself and reports no observation.

items.title: The Gaussian family attains the position-momentum bound in the massive model
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, which assigns the ray of a unit
vector as a pure preparation, the observable and probability postulate P2, and
the massive-particle model postulate P5 read through
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a spinless particle
($s=0$, $r=1$) of mass parameter $m>0$. Assume the Axiom of Choice and the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]),
as required by the spectral probability and moment suppliers used below.
Fix a width $\sigma>0$ and define
$$\psi_{\sigma}(x):=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})},\qquad x\in\mathbb R^{3},$$
with momentum width $\sigma_{p}:=\hbar/\sigma$ and momentum representative
$U\psi_{\sigma}$ under the model's momentum transform $U$. Then:

(i) $\psi_{\sigma}\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ is a unit vector, so
P1 assigns its ray $[\psi_{\sigma}]$ as a pure preparation;
$\psi_{\sigma}\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{k})$ for all
$j,k$, and $P_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=i\hbar\sigma^{-2}x_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$;

(ii) the position outcome law of $Q_{j}$ has density
$(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-t^{2}/\sigma^{2}}$ in the coordinate $t=x_{j}$,
with mean $0$ and variance $\sigma^{2}/2$, so
$\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}Q_{j}=\sigma/\sqrt2$;

(iii) $U\psi_{\sigma}=\psi_{\sigma_{p}}$, that is
$$(U\psi_{\sigma})(p)=(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|p|^{2}/(2\sigma_{p}^{2})};$$
the momentum outcome law of $P_{k}$ has density
$(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-p_{k}^{2}/\sigma_{p}^{2}}$, with mean $0$ and
variance $\sigma_{p}^{2}/2=\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$, so
$\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}P_{k}=\hbar/(\sigma\sqrt2)$;

(iv) for every $j$,
$$\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}Q_{j}\,\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}P_{j}=\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
and the centered vectors are linearly dependent with vanishing real part of
their pairing:
$$Q_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=-\frac{i\sigma^{2}}{\hbar}P_{j}\psi_{\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{Re}\bigl\langle Q_{j}\psi_{\sigma},P_{j}\psi_{\sigma}\bigr\rangle=0,$$
so the equality case of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-relation]] clause (c) is realized.

The computation is one family of preparations in the model; it is not a
characterization of all preparations attaining $\hbar/2$, involves no dynamics,
no detection model and no empirical value.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 3.4.1, printed pages 86-88 (PDF pages 89-91): the Gaussian wavepacket, its position and momentum variances and the saturation Delta x Delta p = hbar/2

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 2.3.2-2.3.3 and Box 2.3, printed pages 27-31 (PDF pages 35-39): the Gaussian packet's momentum-space amplitude, the dispersion product sigma_p sigma = hbar/2 and the Gaussian integral

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', Section 2, printed pages 3-6: the saturation conditions of the uncertainty inequality

The example uses the model's own sharp outcome laws and the cited mathematics; it computes no dynamics, models no measurement, records no empirical value and claims no characterization of all equality states.

items.title: Spin one half: spread identity, incompatible component outcomes and saturated Robertson bounds
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment P6, read for the spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s=\tfrac12$ and $r=2$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the hypotheses of the cited spectral, moment and
Robertson suppliers. Write
$S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ for the model's internal-factor operators of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c), so that
$J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), and let
$\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}$ be the preparation spread of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Then, for every unit
$\psi\in H_{1/2}$:

(a) with $\langle\mathbf S\rangle_{\psi}:=\bigl(\langle S_{x}\psi,\psi\rangle,\langle S_{y}\psi,\psi\rangle,\langle S_{z}\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$\sum_{i\in\{x,y,z\}}\bigl(\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}\bigr)^{2}=\frac{3\hbar^{2}}{4}-\bigl|\langle\mathbf S\rangle_{\psi}\bigr|^{2}\ge\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2},$$
so at least one component satisfies
$\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}\ge\hbar/\sqrt6$; in particular no unit state has all
three component spreads equal to zero;

(b) for every pair of distinct components the spectral projection-valued
measures fail to commute; explicitly, with
$P_{i}^{\pm}:=\tfrac12(I\pm\sigma_{i})$ the spectral projections of $S_{i}$ at
$\pm\hbar/2$,
$$P_{x}^{+}P_{y}^{+}-P_{y}^{+}P_{x}^{+}=\tfrac{i}{2}\sigma_{z}\ne0,$$
and cyclically; consequently no pair of the three components possesses a joint
sharp observable in the sense of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-compatible-sharp-observables-and-joint-law]];

(c) in the state $\psi=f\,e_{1/2}$ with any unit spatial factor
$f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and the basis vector
$e_{1/2}$ of the internal factor,
$$\langle S_{z}\rangle_{\psi}=\frac{\hbar}{2},\qquad \langle S_{x}\rangle_{\psi}=\langle S_{y}\rangle_{\psi}=0,\qquad \Delta_{\psi}S_{x}=\Delta_{\psi}S_{y}=\frac{\hbar}{2},\qquad \Delta_{\psi}S_{z}=0,$$
and $\Delta_{\psi}S_{x}\Delta_{\psi}S_{y}=\hbar^{2}/4=\tfrac12|\langle[S_{x},S_{y}]\psi,\psi\rangle|$,
so the Robertson bound of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] is attained in this state;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, P6,
the stated choice hypotheses and the cited mathematics of the finite internal
matrices acting on $H_{1/2}$. They concern the internal-factor
coupling constants of the model; they assert no laboratory measurement of a
spin component, no Stern-Gerlach apparatus model, no dynamics, no empirical
value and no interpretation of $S_{i}$ as a rotating body or as orbital
angular momentum.

items.physical_scope: The spin-one-half internal factor of the massive particle model: the exact identity for the sum of the three component spreads in every unit state, the resulting lower bound hbar^2/2 and the impossibility of a state with all three component spreads small, the failure of spectral compatibility for every pair of spin components with the explicit projection witness, and the saturation of the Robertson bound in the S_z eigenstates. The statement is a conditional consequence of P1, P2, P5 and P6, under the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice required by the cited spectral and moment suppliers, and the cited finite-dimensional mathematics; it asserts no measurement, apparatus, dynamics, empirical value or claim about angular momentum in space.

items.title: A commutator vanishing on a dense invariant domain does not imply strong spectral commutation
items.statement:
Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space, let $A,B$ be self-adjoint
operators on $H$, and let $D\subseteq D(A)\cap D(B)$ be a dense linear
subspace with $AD\subseteq D(B)$ and $BD\subseteq D(A)$. If $ABu=BAu$ for
every $u\in D$, then the spectral projection-valued measures of $A$ and $B$
strongly commute in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b).

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 9.1, printed pages 181-186 (PDF pages 193-198): self-adjoint boundary conditions of a first-order differential expression on an interval, and the dependence of the spectrum on the boundary condition

Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations (Springer Universitext 2011), Sections 8.1-8.2 printed pages 201-210 and Section 8.4 printed page 227 (PDF pages 216-225 and 242): Sobolev spaces in one dimension, the absolutely continuous representative, and Example 7 on periodic boundary conditions

items.title: Time is not an observable of the framework: the conditional timescale bound
items.statement:
## Why there is no energy-time Robertson pair

**Time is a parameter, not an observable.** The framework's evolution
postulate P4 assigns to an isolated system a self-adjoint energy operator and
the flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH/\hbar)$ with $t$ a real parameter of the curve
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). The framework's
assigned sharp observables are self-adjoint operators with spectral
projection-valued measures and outcome laws
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]); time is not among them:
there is no assigned self-adjoint time operator whose outcome law would enter
the Robertson relation of [[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]], and
this page introduces none. Consequently the expression
$\Delta H\,\Delta t$ is not an instance of the Robertson relation, and the
symbol $\Delta t$ has no definition until a timescale constructed from
observables is specified.

## The conditional timescale bound

**What the framework does support.** The graph-domain Ehrenfest theorem
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-graph-domain-ehrenfest-and-timescale]] is a
conditional mathematical statement about a curve
$\psi:I\to H$ that is $C^{1}$ into the graph norm of a self-adjoint $A$, stays
in $D(AK)$ (and in $D(KA)$ where stated), has unit norm and satisfies
$\psi'=-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}K\psi$. Under those hypotheses, with
$f(t):=\langle A\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ and $f'(t_{0})\ne0$, the timescale
$\tau_{A}(t_{0}):=\Delta A(t_{0})/|f'(t_{0})|$ satisfies
$$\Delta K(t_{0})\,\tau_{A}(t_{0})\ge\frac{\hbar}{2}.$$
With $K=H$ the energy, the Heisenberg-picture theorem identifies $f'(t_{0})$
with the derivative of the mean of the representative observable when $A$ is
bounded and preserves the energy domain,
$A D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subseteq D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$
([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-picture]] clause (c)). Boundedness
alone does not imply this domain-invariance condition. For a domain-qualified,
possibly unbounded $A$, the graph-domain theorem still gives the
Schroedinger-picture derivative stated above, but no Heisenberg-picture
identification is asserted here. The spreads
$\Delta A(t_{0})$ and $\Delta K(t_{0})$ are preparation spreads in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and the theorem's clause (d)
records that when $f'(t_{0})=0$ the quotient supplies no timescale at all.

**What is not claimed.** The timescale $\tau_{A}$ depends on the chosen
observable $A$ and on the state: different choices give different numbers, and
no universal "lifetime" or "duration" of the system is defined. No time
operator, no energy-time Robertson inequality, no claim that an energy
uncertainty is a linewidth and no relation such as $\gamma_{E}\approx\hbar\Gamma$
is asserted by P1-P6; such statements require additional model assumptions
(an apparatus or clock model, a decay model or an analytic continuation) that
are outside this page. The heuristic accounts of measurement disturbance in
the literature are not identities of the framework and are not used as
premises here.

## Remarks

- **Relation to the preparation-spread results.** The timescale bound is a
  Robertson-type estimate applied to the pair (energy, chosen observable)
  along a curve; it does not weaken or strengthen the preparation-spread
  relation of [[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]], which concerns a
  single preparation and two observables.
- **No empirical content.** No measured lifetime, linewidth or energy
  uncertainty is recorded here, and no comparison with data is attempted.

items.title: Preparation spread, apparatus resolution and disturbance are different objects
items.statement:
## Three distinct objects

**Preparation spread.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ and a
preparation $\rho$, the spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that the observable and probability postulate assigns to the pair
$(\rho,A)$: it is a property of the preparation and the assigned observable,
computed from the Born law alone, and it exists only under the stated moment
hypotheses. The inequalities of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] concern these spreads and nothing
else.

**Apparatus resolution or error.** A finite-resolution apparatus is modeled in
this category by a declared instrument with effects and an update rule
([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]];
clause (iv) of P2 and the ideal conditional measurement postulate P3 in the
readings of [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]). Whether a
declared effect family approximates a target observable, and by how much, is a
property of the chosen instrument: the postulates do not attach a universal
error parameter to a sharp observable, and the effects alone do not determine
the update ([[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]]).

**Disturbance.** The state change produced by a measurement is likewise part
of the declared instrument: for the framework's declared ideal sharp
measurement the conditional and discarded-outcome updates are specified in
[[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]], and
they are idealizations, not claims about every apparatus. The framework's
postulates assign no universal disturbance to "a measurement of position" as
such.

## What is and is not asserted

**No conflation.** The Robertson relation bounds the product of two
preparation spreads; it does not bound an apparatus error, it does not bound a
disturbance, and it is not a statement that measuring one quantity "must"
perturb another by a fixed amount. The heuristic accounts of measurement
intrusion in the literature are accordingly used on this page at most as
motivation: the exact statements are the preparation-spread results, and the
identification of a concrete apparatus with a declared instrument is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

**No universal error-disturbance relation is recorded.** This page and the
measurement page contain no theorem of the form "error times disturbance is at
least $\hbar/2$": such a statement would require declared error and
disturbance quantifiers for an instrument and its own proof. What is recorded
here is only the separation of the three objects and the conditional
results actually proved on the two pages.

## Remarks

- **Why the distinction is load-bearing.** An experiment that reports a finite
  resolution, a detection efficiency or a background model is reporting
  apparatus properties; a preparation spread is a model quantity of the state
  and the assigned observable. Agreement of a measured histogram with a
  predicted distribution tests the combined preparation, apparatus and
  observable identification, not the inequality alone.
- **Disturbance is model-dependent.** Two declared instruments with the same
  outcome effects can have different updates and hence different disturbances,
  as [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]]
  records; a disturbance claim must therefore name its instrument.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.4, printed page 15 (PDF page 23): the ideal measurement assumption and the resulting state change

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Chapter 3, printed pages 87-100 (PDF pages 99-112): the probability interpretation of the spectral measure on which the preparation spread is defined

items.physical_scope: A scope and reading remark separating three notions on the uncertainty and compatibility page and the measurement page of the category: the preparation spread of an outcome law, the resolution or error of a declared apparatus, and the disturbance of the preparation produced by a measurement. The remark records that the framework's postulates define the first through the Born law and the second and third only through declared instruments and apparatus models, and that no universal error-disturbance relation, no universal disturbance bound and no empirical result is asserted. It proves nothing itself.

items.title: What the examples companion records and what it does not
items.statement:
## What the companion contains

**One exact model computation.** [[ex-nrqm-uncertainty-gaussian-minimum-spread]]
computes the position and momentum densities and spreads of the Gaussian
family in the spinless massive model and verifies that the product equals
$\hbar/2$ with the centered vectors linearly dependent and their pairing
purely imaginary, realizing the equality case of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-relation]]. It is a statement about
one family of preparations of the model; it contains no dynamics, no detection
model and no measured number, and it does not characterize all equality
states.

**One finite internal-factor deduction.**
[[texp-nrqm-uncertainty-spin-half-incompatibility]] derives the spread
identity $\sum_{i}(\Delta S_{i})^{2}=3\hbar^{2}/4-|\langle\mathbf S\rangle|^{2}$
for the spin-$\tfrac12$ internal factor, the lower bound $\hbar^{2}/2$, the
failure of spectral compatibility for every pair of components, and the
saturation of the Robertson bound in the $S_{z}$ eigenstates. It is a
conditional deduction inside the model's internal factor; it asserts no
Stern-Gerlach apparatus, no dynamics and no measurement.

**One purely mathematical counterexample.**
[[cex-nrqm-uncertainty-commutator-zero-on-a-core-is-not-spectral-compatibility]]
is a statement of pure mathematics about two self-adjoint extensions of the
interval momentum operator: it refutes the implication from a commutator
identity on a dense core to strong spectral commutation. It carries no
physical premise and makes no physical claim.

**Two scope remarks.** [[rem-nrqm-uncertainty-energy-time-caveat]] records
that time is a parameter and not an observable, so no energy-time Robertson
pair exists here and only the conditional timescale bound is available;
[[rem-nrqm-uncertainty-error-disturbance-distinction]] separates preparation
spread, apparatus resolution and disturbance. Both are readings of other
items, not new theorems.

## What it does not contain

**No experiment and no data.** The companion records no preparation
procedure, apparatus, calibration, trial count, count rate, histogram,
uncertainty budget or statistical analysis, and it uses no empirical premise.
Every quantity computed here is a model quantity. Any comparison with data
would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions through the
identification of a preparation and an apparatus with the model's objects, a
tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus
postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), and would
not turn the conditional results into unconditional statements about nature.

**No universal claims.** The Gaussian family is not all preparations; the
spin deduction concerns the internal factor of the model; the counterexample
concerns two specific operators. In particular the companion does not claim
that every state attaining $\hbar/2$ is Gaussian, that every pair of
incompatible components excludes all forms of joint measurement, or that the
timescale bound is a universal energy-time relation.

## Remarks

- **Reading order.** The mathematical items precede the model computations on
  the main page; the companion consumes the main page's items and adds no new
  supplier to them.
- **Status.** As everywhere in this category, agreement of the conditional
  predictions with a laboratory result would be evidence for the combined
  model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework; the companion
  reports no such result.
